thread:
IncidentBot: PAGER: High error rate and repeated fallback loops for EU inference traffic. Severity: P1. Alerts: 1780012345.

Lee (oncall): I'm on it, grabbing context. What customer impact are we seeing?

Ravi (CS): Multiple EU customers reported tool-calling failures and malformed responses starting ~09:12 UTC. Impacting 3 paid tenants, higher error spikes on embeddings->toolchain flows.

Alex (devex): Seeing many requests returning 500 with body: 'incompatible_model_variant: tool_calling_not_supported'. Then the router retries to other region/variant and it loops back.

Maria (sre): Can you paste a few router logs? Need request ids and routing decisions.

Alex (devex): Pasting sanitized excerpts:
```
[09:14:01] route_decision id=abc123 from=eu-west candidate=redwood-v3-16q policy=smart-route -> selected=redwood-v3-16q
[09:14:01] model_launch id=abc123 variant=16q quantized=true tool_calling=false
[09:14:01] inference_error id=abc123 err="tool_calling_not_supported"
[09:14:01] router_retry id=abc123 fallback=us-east-1 candidate=redwood-v3-16fp
[09:14:02] route_decision id=abc123 from=eu-west candidate=redwood-v3-16fp policy=smart-route -> selected=redwood-v3-16fp
[09:14:02] inference_ok id=abc123
[09:14:05] router_redirect id=abc123 back_to=eu-west candidate=redwood-v3-16q
```
We see a back-and-forth: router is preferring local region variant but fallback is incompatible for tool calling and then sends traffic back.

Todd (ml): Root cause looks like the compatibility matrix was updated yesterday to mark 16q as supported for generation, but the tool_calling flag was incorrectly set to false for the quantized variant. The smart-routing policy doesn't check tool_calling compatibility before preferring variant.

Maria (sre): OK, mitigation plan: 1) Stop the loop by disabling smart-route for EU traffic or pinning customers to a compatible variant. 2) Patch compatibility matrix and add pre-check in router. Which is faster?

Lee (oncall): Which can we do quickly? I can flip routing to prefer fp16 in EU.

Jen (ops): I can push a quick policy change: set region_override for eu-* to prefer quality-tier=fp16 for routes that request tool_calling. Command: 
```bash
# temporary policy change
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"scope":"eu","preference":"fp16_for_tool_calling"}' \
  https://controlplane.internal/policies/override
```
I'll run now.

Alex (devex): Before you do, we should pin affected tenants explicitly so other EU customers don't get affected by the override. Ravi can give list of impacted tenants.

Ravi (CS): Impacted tenants: tenant-omega, tenant-sparrow, tenant-lumos. Pin requests submitted.

Lee (oncall): Executing pins:
```bash
# pin tenant-omega to redwood-v3-16fp
redwoodctl pin-model --tenant tenant-omega --model redwood-v3-16fp --reason "mitigation: quant variant incompatible with tool_calling"
```
Pinned tenant-omega. Pinned tenant-sparrow. Pinned tenant-lumos.

Jen (ops): Policy override applied: EU preference = fp16_for_tool_calling. Watchers: telemetry shows error rate dropping from 18% -> 3% in EU over 2 mins.

IncidentBot: Update: Pager acknowledged by Lee (oncall).

Alex (devex): Quick postmortem notes: router lacks a compatibility gate when computing candidate scores. It only considers latency/cost/availability but not feature flags like tool_calling or max_context. That allowed quantized variant selection even when it can't satisfy the request features.

Todd (ml): Confirmed compatibility matrix entry for redwood-v3-16q has tool_calling=false. Yesterday's rollout accidentally marked the variant as 'supported' in the model catalog UI, but the metadata didn't populate to router index. So UI and runtime diverged.

Maria (sre): Are there any customers still failing? Ravi?

Ravi (CS): Customers report degraded but usable. Lumos still had intermittent failures until pinned. Now stable.

Lee (oncall): Next steps for immediate: keep EU override active, monitor for 2 hours, rollback if stable. Add post-incident ticket to: 1) Add router compatibility gate, 2) Add CI that diff model catalog UI vs runtime metadata, 3) Improve telemetry to surface 'candidate_feature_mismatch' counts.

Jen (ops): Creating ticket INF-5412: "Router must validate model variant feature flags (tool_calling, context_length, tokenizer_compat) before routing". Assign Maria + Todd.

Maria (sre): I'll take INF-5412 with Todd. Also creating INF-5413 for 'catalog/runtime metadata parity test' assigned to Alex.

Todd (ml): I'll add a unit test and an integration test to the model onboarding pipeline that rejects variants whose catalog flags and runtime manifest disagree for critical features.

Alex (devex): For on-call runbook: add a step to check 'variant_feature_compatibility' metric and pin as first mitigation.

IncidentBot: NOTE: Page acknowledged and acknowledged_by=Lee (oncall). Duration so far: ~32m.

Ravi (CS): I'll follow up with customers with a timeline and mitigation summary.

Lee (oncall): Handing off to day shift. @Maria please own monitoring for next 2h. I'll update incident page and start timeline.

Maria (sre): Taking over. Will post a short RCA draft in 2 business hours.

Alex (devex): Logs and snippets saved under /incidents/1780012345/artifacts. Will attach compatibility diff and concrete commands used.

Todd (ml): Action items recap:
- (Todd) Add tests to onboarding pipeline (ETA: 5 business days)
- (Maria) Implement router pre-checks (ETA: 3 business days)
- (Alex) CI parity check (ETA: 4 business days)
- (Jen) Keep EU override until QA approves rollback (owner Jen)

Jen (ops): Monitoring steady. No new spikes in last 10m.

Ravi (CS): Customers acknowledged mitigation, asked for postmortem and preventative timeline.

Lee (oncall): Closing the active pager; incident remains open for RCA and followups. Will update incident epic.

IncidentBot: Pager closed by Lee (oncall). Final status: mitigated -> routing override + pins.

(END of thread)
